title: Complex analytic derivatives and their algebraic rules
statement: Let $E,F,G$ be finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] normed complex vector spaces. Here complex analytic means locally represented by convergent complex power series. If $U\subseteq E$ is open and $f:E\to F$ is complex analytic at every point of $U$, then $x\mapsto Df(x)$ is complex analytic at every point of $U$, with values in the space of continuous complex-linear maps $E\to F$. At points where the indicated derivatives exist, $D(f+g)=Df+Dg$, $D(uv)=u\,Dv+v\,Du$ for scalar-valued $u,v$, and $D(g\circ f)(x)=Dg(f(x))\circ Df(x)$. The derivative of a constant is zero and the derivative of the identity is the identity linear map. A continuous complex-linear map $L:E\to F$ has derivative $L$ at every point. For a finite family $f_j:E\to\mathbf C$ with derivatives $L_j$ at $x$, the tuple $(f_j)_j$ has derivative $v\mapsto(L_j(v))_j$ at $x$.
